land.text: Beloozero, which 'became independent in 1238 during the Mongol invasions of Kievan Rus'

predecessors.note: The page has Rostov and Beloozero under Novgorod, then governed from Kiev in the late 11th century, and Beloozero independent in 1238; Cliopatria's Rostov-Suzdal row ends in 1240.

land.text: Beloozero, administered by Ivan Kalita's namestniks 'instead of the princes' and 'subjugated by Muscovy' in 1389

successors.note: Cliopatria's Beloozero shape ends 1343 and 41 of its 42 cells are in the Moscow shape of 1344. The page keeps nominal princes (Dmitry Donskoy's son Andrey and his son Mikhail) until the formal annexation in 1485 or 1486.

capitals.name: Beloozero (Belozersk)
capitals.note: 'Its capital was Beloozero (now Belozersk).' Coordinates are the modern town's; the gazetteer lacks the name.

correction.text: the basin of Lake Beloye, the lower streams of the Sheksna River and Lake Kubenskoye, Gleb's territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for 1238-1293. The page gives Gleb's territory (ca. 1238-1278) as 'the basin of Lake Beloye, the lower streams of the Sheksna River, and Lake Kubenskoye'; no area. Cliopatria's 1294 shape holds 4 of the 5 cells of Lake Beloye and part of the Sheksna but only 1 cell of Lake Kubenskoye on its eastern edge, so the lake is added.

10,010 km2 (42 cells) for 1294-1332, centred at 38.0 E, 60.3 N round Lake Beloye. The page gives no area or later extent; 'The duchy had lost its former significance by the early 14th century.' Lake Kubenskoye, named for Gleb's time, is mostly outside the shape.

Same cells as 1294 (10,010 km2) for 1333-1343. The page dates nothing in these years except that Ivan Kalita (d. 1340) 'was already appointing namestniks of Beloozero who administered the principality instead of the princes'.

region.text: the basin of Lake Beloye, the lower streams of the Sheksna River and Lake Kubenskoye, Gleb's territory

ledger.note: 1238: Beloozero becomes an independent principality under Prince Gleb. Infobox 'Established: 1238'; it 'became independent in 1238 during the Mongol invasions of Kievan Rus'; 'Prince Gleb was the first prince of Beloozero (ca. 1238-1278)'; his territory 'embraced the basin of Lake Beloye, the lower streams of the Sheksna River, and Lake Kubenskoye'.

region.text: the Beloozero country, administered by Moscow's namestniks

ledger.note: 1343 (last year of Cliopatria's shape): the Beloozero country passes to Moscow's direct administration. The page dates none of it: 'In the first half of the 14th century, Ivan Kalita ... was already appointing namestniks of Beloozero who administered the principality instead of the princes'; the Ivan I page credits Ivan I with 'purchasing the principalities of Beloozero, Galich and Uglich' and adds 'some scholars do not believe that Ivan actually purchased those principalities'. The Moscow dossier records the gain in 1344, the first year of its shape.

The principality ends as an independent state under Ivan Kalita's namestniks; the date is Cliopatria's. The page also says 'In 1389, it was subjugated by Muscovy' (Dmitry Donskoy then gave it to his son Andrey) and that nominal princes lasted 'until it was formally annexed in 1485', while its other passage and the infobox say 1486; the land is drawn as Moscow's from 1344.

certainty.note: The page gives the lake basins, not a boundary; the forest frontier with Novgorod and Vladimir-Suzdal is approximate throughout.

sources.title: Ivan I of Moscow
sources.note: Beloozero among the purchases credited to Ivan I (undated, doubted).

notes: Single Cliopatria row (1294-1343, two identical shapes). The state is dated 1238-1343 here: the page's own end dates (1389 'subjugated by Muscovy', 1485/1486 'formally annexed', internally inconsistent) describe a nominal principality under Moscow, while Cliopatria hands the land to Moscow in 1344 and the page has Moscow's namestniks governing 'instead of the princes' in the first half of the 14th century; the end year is Cliopatria's (confidence 1). The Moscow dossier shows the land as Moscow's from 1344 to 1546. The princes 'Gleb ... (ca. 1238-1278)' married a daughter of Sartaq (Beloozero page); no later prince is dated on the page, so no ruler list is given. Names the gazetteer lacks: Beloozero (Belozersk), used in capitals as coordinates only. Page budget: the Beloozero page and the Ivan I page (read for the Moscow dossier); no page failed.
